articles.title: On the bubble? Giants WR Odell Beckham Jr., Steelers RB Kaleb Johnson among those who might not make 53-man roster
articles.summary: Here are some of the notable names that could be in danger of being cut or perhaps traded as teams finalize their regular-season rosters.
articles.body:
It's not a comfortable time of year for many NFL players.

On Sunday, teams must cut down their rosters to 53 players. That makes for some tough decisions. It also has front offices scouring the bottoms of rosters, trying to find intriguing players they might want to pick up if they're cut, or acquire in trades just before the roster deadline.

Here are some of the notable names that could be in danger of being cut or perhaps traded as teams get down to 53 players:

Calvin Austin III's season-ending knee injury could help Beckham, who is trying to complete a cool comeback story with the Giants. Beckham hasn't played for the Giants since 2018, and didn't play at all last season. He got a shot at age 33 to make the team. He has had some fun throwback highlights in camp

Still, the Giants aren't making decisions based on nostalgia. Does Beckham fit in their receiver room? He'd need to be a part of the receiver rotation since it seems farfetched that he would contribute on special teams. A dropped touchdown in the second preseason game couldn't have helped his case.

It would be a great story, but it's far from a guarantee. And if Beckham makes it, it probably means 2023 third-round draft pick Jalin Hyatt does not (though both could end up not making the roster).

"I mean, I love Odell. I do," Giants head coach John Harbaugh said , via Giants Wire. "What he's doing, what he's fighting for, I don't know how it's going to turn out. It's going to turn out the way it turns out, based on what happens. But to see his fight, his determination, his humility. He's got his son in camp the other day, you know, he's doing it for his son. You know, that just, as a friend, that makes me really proud of him."

It was surprising to see Johnson play behind Travis Homer and Lew Nichols in the first preseason game. Johnson didn't appear in the game until the second half. That signifies he is fifth on the depth chart at best.

Johnson was an intriguing third-round pick a year ago. A mistake in the fourth quarter against Seattle in Week 2, mishandling a kickoff return that was recovered by the Seahawks in the end zone for a touchdown, was a blunder he never recovered from. He finished his rookie season with 69 rushing yards on 28 carries. A new coaching staff came in and Johnson was buried even further on the depth chart. Teams don't usually keep fifth-string tailbacks on the roster.

McCarthy, the 10th pick of the 2024 draft who struggled last season, is unlikely to be cut. He also might lose a competition with Carson Wentz to be the Vikings' backup quarterback and be on the third string by Week 1. If there is any player that desperately needs a trade and a new start, it's McCarthy. It can't be ruled out.

Coleman is another player who isn't getting cut, but would a trade be that surprising? When the team owner is assigning blame for drafting you , you're in trouble with the organization. Coleman, a 2024 second-round draft pick, still has time to become an impact receiver, whether it's in Buffalo or not.

Kirk missed almost all of training camp with a calf injury. The 49ers have a clear top three at receiver in Mike Evans, Deebo Samuel and rookie De'Zhaun Stribling. Kirk doesn't have an obvious role, and that could put his roster spot in jeopardy. Kirk could also start the season on injured reserve.

Hamlin seems to have played his way onto the roster this summer, according to ESPN's Alaina Getzenberg . Still, he's a backup safety and 28 years old. Hamlin is likely to make the BIlls again, but he'll want the official news to make sure.

Dillon, who played four seasons with the Packers and last season with the Eagles, is trying to make the Panthers' roster. He has been working on special teams to help his case. That, and Chuba Hubbard's hamstring injury that kept him out for a lot of camp, could help him get a spot.

Appearing on the transaction wire is nothing new to the famously well-traveled Johnson. Johnson is 40 and always seems to find a backup job somewhere. The Bengals will have Joe Burrow and Joe Flacco on the active roster but likely have Johnson on speed dial or the practice squad.

Browns QB Dillon Gabriel or Taylen Green

Teams don't generally keep four quarterbacks. Green could be an exception because he's a stellar athlete who could be used in gadget roles. It seems likely the Browns keep Deshaun Watson, Shedeur Sanders, Gabriel and Green, but it's unconventional and perhaps they would answer the phone if anyone calls about Dillon, a third-round pick last year.

Mingo was struggling as a young second-round pick for the Panthers when the Cowboys suddenly traded a fourth-round pick for him. It was panned by everyone and it hasn't worked out; he has just six catches for 71 yards since he was acquired during the 2024 season. The Cowboys' top four receivers are set, and Mingo is on the bubble to make the roster.

Elam was a first-round pick of the Bills in 2022. He didn't work out there and hasn't found footing elsewhere. He hasn't moved far up the Chiefs' depth chart and it seems likely he'll be a free agent again soon.

Colson seemed like a great fit as a third-round pick of the Chargers in 2024. He was joining his college coach, Jim Harbaugh. But Colson has had injury issues, has started only one game and has been playing with backups late in preseason games this year. It would be early to give up on him, but it's possible.

Dolphins WRs Jalen Reagor and Terrace Marshall Jr.

The Dolphins tried adding some receivers who were highly drafted a few years ago. Reagor was a former first-round pick and Marshall was a second-round pick, and neither panned out. They probably won't pan out in Miami either, but Reagor's ability as a returner gives him a shot to stick.

Saints QB Zach Wilson or Spencer Rattler

Will the Saints keep three quarterbacks? If not, either Wilson or Rattler have to go. Wilson had been behind Rattler for much of camp, but he started over Rattler in the second preseason game. Wilson and Rattler made mistakes in that game, so neither should feel like they're roster locks.

Tracy has been a productive back, but there's a new coaching staff and Tracy hasn't had a good camp or preseason. In the Giants' first preseason game he missed a pass block that led to a big hit on Jaxson Dart, and in the second preseason game he fumbled. The Giants signed Najee Harris, which makes the running back room even more crowded.

It seems unlikely that Rudolph will get cut, but it's also not typical for a team to keep four quarterbacks. Aaron Rodgers and recent draftees Will Howard and Drew Allar seem like locks. If Rudolph is on the roster it probably means the Steelers will be carrying four quarterbacks.

Cam Ward is the Titans' starter. Mitchell Trubisky is the backup. Maybe Levis stays on as the Titans' third quarterback, but a new coaching staff that didn't draft Levis would have to see the value in using a roster spot on him.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 Mock Draft Tips and Latest Consensus Rankings
articles.summary: The final week of the 2026 NFL preseason is underway, and real, meaningful football is nearly back. For fantasy enthusiasts, this means that we are entering the prime drafting window.
articles.body:
The final week of the 2026 NFL preseason is underway, and real, meaningful football is nearly back. For fantasy enthusiasts, this means that we are entering the prime drafting window.

Drafting after the August 30 roster cuts will be ideal, as managers will then have a clearer idea of player roles and roster statuses. Between now and then, though, they can prepare for their live drafts by running a few mocks and collecting the data.

Of course, to get the most out of mock drafts, it's best to execute them with a purpose. Here, you'll find some mock-drafting tips, a three-round mock conducted with FantasyPros' Mock Draft Simulator , and a look at FantasyPros ' latest consensus point-per-reception (PPR) rankings.

The biggest piece of advice we can offer about mock drafting is to take notes, track data, and pay close attention to where your favorite players are being taken. This information can help you create a personalized draft board that is more beneficial than even the latest consensus rankings.

The trick is to make sure that your mock draft parameters—roster makeup, scoring rules, flex options, etc.—match your actual draft perfectly. Under those guidelines, you may find that certain players you have circled pre-draft are going higher or lower than their consensus average draft position (ADP) might suggest.

When creating a personalized draft board, it's also a good idea to track any sleepers you've identified and wish to target. Has that high-upside rookie RB drifted upward from Round 12 toward Round 9? That's great information to have on draft day and can help prevent missing out on a prospect you love.

Experiment With Different Strategies, but Focus on RBs Early or Zero RB

Managers should try mock drafting from different positions, even if they know their draft slot, in order to get a feel for how other drafters may approach things. They should also try out different strategies to identify a preferred approach and a strong Plan B.

Whether you want to target a high-volume receiver like Ja'Marr Chase early in Round 1 or have your heart set on two elite RBs, there's a good chance that other managers will make that plan difficult.

In 2026, there's going to be a massive drop-off in RB talent after the initial wave. Players like James Cook, De'Von Achane, and Chase Brown form a solid group just under the elites—high-volume backs like Jahmyr Gibbs and Bijan Robinson—but second-tier backs like Josh Jacobs and D'Andre Swift are far less appealing.

We'd recommend trying different strategies that yield at least one high-level RB within the first two rounds and two out of the first three. The WRs available in Rounds 4-8 are likely to have much more value than the RBs available in that range.

However, we'd also recommend trying a few zero-RB strategies as a backup plan. If there's an early run at the position, managers might benefit from snapping up top-tier WRs and TEs while looking for RB value after other starting lineups have been filled.

For example, getting RJ Harvey ( draft rank of 107) in Round 9 might yield far more value than taking Travis Etienne Jr. ( draft rank of 47) five rounds higher.

Lastly, it's important to run as many mock drafts as possible in order to get the most accurate collection of data.

Even one or two mocks can help managers get a feel for how they want to draft—and help get used to the panic of being on the clock right after your favorite player got sniped. However, a larger sample size will always paint a more accurate picture of where players are being valued and how strategies are working.

articles.title: Inspiring story on mental strength: “No one really sees pro athletes behind the scenes. They don't know how hard they work”- How Patrick Mahomes built a mindset beyond natural talent
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes became famous for throws that seemed almost impossible. Behind that effortless style, however, sits a lesson he learned long before be.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes became famous for throws that seemed almost impossible. Behind that effortless style, however, sits a lesson he learned long before becoming an NFL superstar. As a child, Mahomes saw professional athletes prepare when nobody was watching. Those quiet hours changed how he viewed success, teaching him that natural ability can open the door, but repetition, preparation and discipline keep an athlete at the top.Patrick Mahomes learned about hard work before becoming an NFL starMahomes shared the insight in an ESPN profile published on October 10, 2018, during his spectacular first season as the Kansas City Chiefs' starting quarterback. Kevin Seifert's article, titled “‘Turbo Andy’ got his guy: Inside the Reid-Mahomes masterpiece,” examined the connection between Mahomes and head coach Andy Reid while also looking at the experiences that shaped the young quarterback.The most revealing part of the story had nothing to do with Mahomes' powerful arm.It began with his childhood.Mahomes grew up around professional baseball because his father, Pat Mahomes Sr., spent more than a decade pitching in Major League Baseball. During the summer, Patrick would accompany his father to big league ballparks. He got to see professional players up close, but the experience quickly became about more than watching stars perform.He watched them prepare.One example stayed with him. Alex Rodriguez, one of baseball's biggest stars at the time, would repeatedly hit balls off a tee before games. To a young Mahomes, that was striking. Rodriguez was already an elite hitter. Yet he still spent time working on one of the simplest drills in baseball.That observation shaped Mahomes' understanding of greatness.He later explained, “No one really sees pro athletes behind the scenes. They don't know how hard they work.”The larger point of his comment was clear. Fans usually see the finished product. They see the touchdown, the home run, the highlight and the celebration. They rarely see the repetitions that come first.For Mahomes, that distinction became an important part of his own approach.Alex Rodriguez showed Patrick Mahomes why basics matterThe lesson Mahomes took from Rodriguez was not simply that professional athletes work hard. It was that even the best players continue returning to the fundamentals.Mahomes specifically pointed to Rodriguez's use of a batting tee. The drill looked basic, especially for someone of Rodriguez's stature. But that was exactly why it mattered.Elite athletes do not abandon simple exercises once they become successful. They often become more committed to them.That idea is easy to overlook because professional sports are built around spectacular moments. A quarterback launches a 50-yard touchdown pass and fans remember the throw. They do not see the countless hours spent studying defensive schemes, reviewing film, repeating footwork or learning how to recognize patterns.Mahomes understood this difference early.His father's own routine reinforced the lesson. After games, Pat Mahomes Sr. would return to his notes and study opposing hitters. While Patrick might go play video games or spend time with friends, his father continued preparing.The contrast showed Mahomes that preparation does not end simply because the game is over.That mindset would later become part of his football routine.Patrick Mahomes applied the lesson to his own preparationBy the time Mahomes reached the NFL, he had already developed an appreciation for studying the details that most people never notice.In the ESPN profile, he explained that he carried the lessons from his childhood into his own film study. He described reviewing game plans repeatedly, including material that had already been covered, because familiarity should never become an excuse to stop paying attention.That approach mattered as Mahomes adjusted to the NFL.His talent was obvious. His arm strength was extraordinary. His ability to throw from different platforms made him one of the most exciting young quarterbacks in football.But Andy Reid and the Chiefs needed more than physical ability.During Mahomes' pre-draft visit to Kansas City in 2017, the coaching staff tested his ability to absorb information. Reid taught him a series of plays, formations, protections and calls. Mahomes then returned to the room and essentially recreated the offense on the whiteboard.Chiefs assistant Brad Childress later summed up the mentality that separates elite players from everyone else: “They're not great because they're great. They work to be great.”That observation fits closely with Mahomes' own childhood lesson.The hidden work behind Patrick Mahomes' successMahomes' career has since become filled with spectacular plays, records and championships. Yet the lesson from his early years remains relevant because it explains something that highlights cannot show.Greatness can look effortless from the outside.It rarely feels effortless to the person doing the work.Mahomes learned that from watching professional baseball players prepare when the cameras were not focused on them. Rodriguez did not need to prove that he was a great hitter every time he stepped onto a field. Instead, he kept refining the smallest parts of his craft.Mahomes adopted the same principle.His own preparation involves film study, repetition and attention to detail. He has spoken about reviewing material every day and making sure he understands every aspect of a game plan rather than assuming he already knows enough.That is perhaps the most powerful part of his message.Fans often see confidence. They see creativity. They see the no-look passes, the sidearm throws and the plays that appear to happen instinctively.Mahomes sees something else.He sees the work that makes those moments possible.His quote from the 2018 ESPN profile therefore carries a lesson that extends beyond football. Success often hides its own process. The strongest performers can make difficult things appear ordinary because they have repeated them so many times.That was the lesson a young Mahomes absorbed while watching his father and some of baseball's biggest stars.Years later, it became part of the foundation of his own career.The spectacular plays may be what make Patrick Mahomes famous. The unseen work is what helps explain why he can keep producing them.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Man who masqueraded as 49ers player facing federal charges in alleged wire fraud scheme that exploited women
articles.summary: He and another man are accused of defrauding at least 26 victims of more than $1.3 million, according to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon...
articles.body:
A man who adopted "fictitious personas," one of which notably was that of a fake San Francisco 49ers player, is part of a duo that's been arrested and charged for defrauding several women of more than $1.3 million, according to the U.S. Attorney's office in the District of Oregon .

The FBI arrested 35-year-old Daejon Love and 18-year-old Taylor Jamie Chan on Monday in Boise, Idaho, where they were apprehended upon meeting at the Boise Airport. They're facing a pair of federal charges: conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud, as detailed in a statement released this week by the U.S. Attorney's office that references court documents.

Love, who the U.S. Attorney's office says repeatedly posed as a Niners player or as a wealthy real estate investor, and Chan, who the U.S. Attorney's office says acted as Love's financial adviser, allegedly accrued the aforementioned sum by exploiting at least 26 victims. Those are the ones the FBI has identified, and the bureau believes there are "many more."

The alleged scheme spanned four years, beginning in February 2022. Love and Chan targeted women in California, Oregon, Washington and Idaho, most of whom Love met through dating apps, prosecutors said. Love has used several names — including Jon Love, Daejon Love, Avril Lyto Love and Jordan Love — while carrying out the caper, per the U.S. Attorney's office.

"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office statement said. "Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."

"Love convinced many of the victims they were in sincere romantic relationships with Love, that he was a sophisticated investor, and that Chan was his investment adviser who helped Love grow a fortune worth tens of millions of dollars," the U.S. Attorney's Office statement said.

"Love had romantic relationships with many of the victims and told them he wanted to build wealth and a future together. Love advertised nonexistent investment vehicles and claimed these investments would generate massive returns for both him and his victims."

Phony bank and investment accounts and balances, created via phone applications, allegedly allowed Love to strengthen the validity of the ploy. Chan and Love even held three-way FaceTimes to flaunt falsified investment gains to whichever victim was on the call, according to the U.S. Attorney's office.

Victims sent Love and Chan money with the intent that it would be deployed for fruitful investments overseen by the tandem, prosecutors said.

"Once victims had no more money to invest, or if they asked too many questions, Love blocked communication with them but kept their money," the U.S. Attorney's office statement said.

"Of the victims identified and interviewed, none reported receiving any proceeds, returns on their principle, or investment account information, after sending Love and Chan money."

At the time of Love and Chan's arrest, Love was in Idaho to meet new victims, per investigators.

articles.title: Falcons QB Tua Tagovailoa booed by Dolphins fans as Miami pays price for failed relationship
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa completed 7 of 8 passes against his former team but still hasn't locked down the Atlanta Falcons starting job over Michael Penix Jr.
articles.body: As reunions go, Tua Tagovailoa’s return to South Florida as an Atlanta Falcon against his former Miami Dolphins teammates was not exactly a happy one. Dysfunctional is a better word for it. For six seasons, Tagovailoa and the Dolphins tried to make it work. They failed. DOLPHINS NOT GOING TO 'THROW IN THE TOWEL AND JUST REBUILD' BUT THAT COMES WITH HIGHER EXPECTATIONS Tagovailoa was set back by some coaches who didn’t like him and injuries that too often overshadowed him, so he never reached his goal of becoming the face of the franchise. And the Dolphins never came close to reaching the championship level they expected when they drafted Tagovailoa in the top five in 2020 and paid him like a top-five quarterback in 2024. The failures resulted in a divorce during the offseason and this exhibition game at Hard Rock Stadium was the first time the couple happened to be at the same place at the same time since the split. And guess what? Everybody believes they're better off after the separation. But no one is at this stage better off after the separation. DOLPHINS CONSULTANT TROY AIKMAN WILL BE LIMITED IN MNF ROLE LIKE RAIDERS MINORITY OWNER TOM BRADY IS ON FOX Tagovailoa is trying to earn a starting job with the Falcons and the fact he came into this game without yet having done so speaks to his failing since training camp began. Because Tagovailoa has basically been competing only against himself while Michael Penix Jr. has been limited in practices as he makes his way back from a 2025 knee surgery. And, yet, with his only significant competition sidelined and the path to the starting job clear, Tagovailoa hasn't been able to lock the job down. The Dolphins? They got rid of Tagovailoa this offseason despite the fact he would be costing them some $55 million in salary in 2026 alone. There's another bill coming next year. The Dolphins were so over this relationship they paid Tagovailoa to go away. And where has that left them? The Tagovailoa move was part of a systematic divestment from talent in order to "solve the salary cap problem" the previous administration got the franchise into. MIAMI DOLPHINS ENTER FULL REBUILD WITH MALIK WILLIS AT QUARTERBACK AND JEFF HAFLEY AS HEAD COACH The Dolphins are now perhaps the least talented team in the NFL as they prepare for a season in which they will be rebuilding for the 1,387th time in the past decade. So here we were on Friday night: Team Rebuild versus Quarterback Not Good Enough. The scene played out in front of a sparse crowd at Hard Rock that mustered enough emotion to boo for the quarterback they once believed would win them a championship. The Sadness Bowl. And, fittingly, nobody really won. Tagovailoa played well enough, completing 7 of 8 passes. But it wasn't actually good. The Dolphins, resting their talent-needy starting defense, fought with backups that will provide substandard depth this season. And the sparing between a QB who is lacking against backups who are lacking was, well, lacking. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Tagovailoa completed 3 of 4 passes on his first drive, with the only incompletion on a throwaway. The Falcons scored a touchdown that drive. But that last paragraph reads more impressively than it looked because the dynamic 43-yard completion from Tagovailoa to Kyle Pitts that highlighted the drive was actually a 4-yard pitch on a screen that the tight end turned into a big run against a scattered defense. On his second drive, Tagovailoa fumbled the snap from center and the Dolphins recovered. And another drive later, running back Brian Robinson fumbled and, once again, the Miami defense recovered. So, good on the Miami defense that is going to get steamrolled once the regular-season begins. And good on Tagovailoa, who still hasn’t done enough to win the Falcons’ starting quarterback job despite facing little healthy competition until this week, when Penix Jr. was fully cleared to practice. articles.title: New Seahawks owner Vinod Khosla defends Steelers fandom after saying he still watches all of their games
articles.summary: No one ask him about Super Bowl XL.
articles.body:
Vinod Khosla, the new owner of the Seattle Seahawks, might have a made the mistake of being too honest while introducing himself to his team's fanbase.

Speaking with reporters on Thursday, the day after the NFL's owners unanimously approved his $9.612 billion purchase of the Seahawks , Khosla discussed his past NFL fandom. Specifically, he confirmed he rooted for a team other than the Seahawks before buying them.

That team wasn't the San Francisco 49ers, whom Khosla purchased a 3% stake in alongside his son last year (which he will now be selling).

No, it's the Pittsburgh Steelers, the NFL's dominant team when Khosla entered the United States decades ago. He said still considers himself a fan of the team and watches every game:

"I happened to come to this country in '76 when the Steelers were winning Super Bowls, so actually I was originally, and still am, a big Steelers fan, also. Little known fact, but I still watch all the Steelers games too."

That one answer drew quite a bit of interest, so much so that Khosla decided to further explain himself on social media the next day. He insisted he will always want the Seahawks to win and complained about the media's reaction to his comments.

"Reporters will make every molehill into a mountain just to get column inches to write or video minutes. What's wrong with admitting my 1976-78 period in Pittsburgh (CMU) got me excited about the NFL? I still watch their games doesn't mean I won't unconditionally ALWAYS as owner, want the @Seahawks to win and have every edge up, EVERY TIME over every other team!!!! Zero questions!!! At the other end is a set of teams I always want to lose every advantage. But happy to have the sports writer getting more column inches and fill their pages. You are welcome. Apologies in advance for my very transparent style."

Khosla obviously wouldn't be the first person to have dual rooting interests in the NFL. We're just dealing with the rare owner who does not care if fans know he has another team he still loves. That's ultimately up to him, but you could forgive Seahawks fans for being a little more wary of what this era will look like.

Khosla's tenure as owner will ultimately be decided by the product on the field and the conduct of the organization. In the meantime, let's just hope he doesn't bring up Super Bowl XL too much in the Pacific Northwest.

articles.title: John Harbaugh Reveals If Odell Beckham Jr. Has Done Enough to Make NFL Roster After Giants Preseason
articles.summary: New York Giants coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence in Odell Beckham Jr. but came short of confirming the wide receiver has earned a roster spot after Friday's preseason finale against the New York Jets.
articles.body:
New York Giants coach John Harbaugh expressed confidence in Odell Beckham Jr. but came short of confirming the wide receiver has earned a roster spot after Friday's preseason finale against the New York Jets.

"I think he has done enough to make an NFL roster for sure," Harbaugh said Friday about Beckham (h/t Fox Sports' Ralph Vacchiano). "He's played well. He's gotten better as camp's gone along, and I think he deserves credit for that."

Landing spots for NFL players already cut

The Giants signed Beckham in June and will need to decide whether to keep him by the 53-man roster deadline this Sunday at 6 p.m. ET.

Harbaugh said Wednesday he thought this week had been Beckham's best of training camp.

Beckham followed that up Friday by making three catches on six targets for 53 yards in preseason action against the Jets. He also came close to what could have been a 73-yard touchdown after getting open for a deep ball from Jameis Winston.

"It would mean everything," Beckham said about potentially making the Giants roster on the in-game broadcast . "It would be my dream. This is where I started. There's no place I want to give my whole heart to, more than anything else in the world, is this place right here."

Beckham continued after the game: "I'm super grateful for the opportunity, and at this point, it's in God's hands.

"I know that I have a good feeling about myself. I feel like there's ball to be played, there's plays to be made."

Beckham, who will turn 34 in November, played three Pro Bowl seasons with the Giants between 2014 and 2016 before his career was derailed by injuries.

The wide receiver last played in the NFL during the 2024 season, during which he appeared in nine games but saw minimal usage with the Miami Dolphins.

He did not sign with any team during the 2025 season, which he started out by serving a six-game suspension for failing the NFL's performance-enhancing drug policy.

Beckham is now trying to make his NFL comeback in a wide receiver room that just lost receiver Calvin Austin III to a season-ending torn right ACL .

"It just means that the next guy steps up and fills that role. We have to readjust," Harbaugh said Wednesday about Austin's injury.

Harbaugh will now have to decide if Beckham's training camp and Austin's injury, combined with preseason struggles from Braxton Berrios, are enough to justify keeping Beckham around for when the Giants open the regular season Sept. 13 against the visiting Dallas Cowboys.

articles.title: 12 toughest cuts from our final Saints 53-man roster predictions
articles.summary: A couple of draft picks, rookie fan-favorites, and plucky veterans weren't able to catch on in our final New Orleans Saints 53-man roster predictions.
articles.body:
This year's NFL roster cuts deadline falls on 5 p.m. CT on Sunday, Aug. 30, giving all 32 teams a quick turnaround between their final preseason game and dozens of tough visits to the office. Like each of their rivals, the New Orleans Saints must cut their rosters down from 90 players to just 53 of them. It's one of the harshest days on the league's calendar.

Some decisions are more difficult than others. Guys have competed hard all summer, fighting through injuries and pushing against competition from other pros who want to make the cut just as badly as they do. But the reality is that just 53 players can make the team. Here were our toughest decisions in trying to predict how the Saints will approach roster cuts .

Wilson flashed the same potential that made him the No. 2 overall draft pick at times this summer, but those flashes were too few and far between for him to be our QB2 (at least so long as Spencer Rattler is around). Even if he can dress out on game days with the emergency QB3 rule, it's not worth burning a roster spot on him. It wasn't worth doing that for Jake Haener, either.

This isn't exactly another Boston Scott situation, but it's not far off from that, either. Neal just hasn't been able to stay healthy. He missed long stretches of his rookie year with hamstring issues and those same injuries have plagued him this summer. He may be a reliable third-down back with real chops in pass protection, but he simply hasn't been available enough to win a roster spot with those skills. Hopefully he can catch on with the practice squad or just heal up for a month or two on injured reserve.

Austin had one more target in team drills (22) than Means did (21) this summer, and his team-first attitude has won over some fans. But the additions the Saints have made in the receiving corps are pushing guys like him onto the practice squad. That's not a bad thing, in the big picture, but it's a setback for Austin as he tries to get his own career off the ground.

Bell has also been targeted 21 times throughout training camp, but he hasn't been quite as productive or consistent (six of those passes went his way in a single session). He's another good option for the practice squad as an experienced pro who knows the playbook well.

It's been another solid summer for Welch, who consistently drew targets in team drills throughout training camp and showcased soft hands in the preseason games, but he hasn't made enough strides as a blocker to make the cut. There's potential here if he could put everything together.

Simpkins was a fan-favorite last summer as a rookie free agent, and it looked like he could have taken a larger role on offense as Erik McCoy's backup after switching to center full-time. Instead, he's been bumped down the depth chart before losing the last week of practice while in concussion protocol. You'd like to get him back on the practice squad but this has still been a rough preseason for Simpkins.

Neither Smyth nor Tanner Brown were able to win the kicker competition this summer, but Smyth's status as an International Pathway Player means he can hang around on the practice squad without taking a roster spot. He has obvious talent, he just needs more experience. Another season of development could be good for him.

Two different coaching staffs have had plenty of time to evaluate Boyd at practice and chosen to play others ahead of him, even while he's graded out well in the preseason. For whatever reason the moments we've seen haven't carried over day-to-day, and this could be the end of the line for him in New Orleans despite a thin depth chart on the interior defensive line.

Heldman quickly built up a fanbase after notching a couple of sacks in the first preseason game; he just couldn't keep that momentum going. He spent most of the summer on the third-team defense and projects well as a fit for the practice squad. He did leave the Cowboys game late with an injury, so look out for an update on his status.

Rumph was a very important player in Brandon Staley's defense last season and it says a lot that he was brought back and cross-trained at off-ball linebacker after rushing off the edge. He's lost a lot of time to an ankle injury but likely would have made the team if healthy.

The numbers game just wasn't in Davison's favor. He's done everything asked of him on defense and special teams, but it hasn't been enough to separate himself from more-accomplished pros. He's another practice squad candidate if he clear waivers.

It's always disappointing to see a draft pick not make the team, even if he's a seventh rounder. There are just different expectations for guys who hear their name called during the event. Hall is a safe pick to return on the practice squad unless another team claims him off of waivers.

articles.title: LaFleur Says He Fully Anticipates Packers Keeping Josh Jacobs While Charges Are Pending
articles.summary: GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur says there are no plans for the team to release running back Josh Jacobs, who faces two misdemeanor charges stemming from what police have described as a physical confrontation with his girlfriend.
articles.body:
GREEN BAY, Wis. (AP) — Green Bay Packers coach Matt LaFleur says there are no plans for the team to release running back Josh Jacobs, who faces two misdemeanor charges stemming from what police have described as a physical confrontation with his girlfriend.

"I fully anticipate him being a member of our team," LaFleur said Friday night after the Packers closed their preseason schedule with a 42-38 victory over the Arizona Cardinals.

The Brown County (Wisconsin) District Attorney's office filed misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property against Jacobs on Thursday. The charges arose from an incident that took place three months ago.

When he was asked about Jacobs' potential availability for the Packers' Sept. 13 season opener at Minnesota, LaFleur replied that "I can't really comment on that because I don't know."

Jacobs was arrested May 26 after police were called to his home to investigate a disturbance, and he was released from jail the next day.

Jacobs' lawyers — David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld, and Clarence F. Duchac III — issued a statement Thursday acknowledging the charges and noting that they "do not include domestic violence."

"The allegations will be addressed in court, and not in the media," they said. "Mr. Jacobs respects the District Attorney's office and the process it followed."

The NFL has said it is monitoring the case. The Packers said they were aware of the charges and would continue to cooperate with the NFL.

Jacobs rushed for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns last season. That followed a 2024 season in which Jacobs ran for 1,329 yards and 15 touchdowns while earning his third Pro Bowl selection.

Running backs behind Jacobs on Green Bay's depth chart include MarShawn Lloyd, Pierre Strong Jr. and Chris Brooks.

Lloyd stayed healthy throughout this preseason, but injuries have caused the 2024 third-round pick to play just one game over the last two seasons. Strong spent last season on Green Bay's practice squad but has 499 career yards rushing. Brooks ran for 106 yards on 27 carries last season while contributing primarily on special teams.

articles.title: Jordan Love Called Plays for Packers in 2nd Half of Preseason Win vs. Cardinals, LaFleur Reveals
articles.summary: Jordan Love still has many years of playing in the NFL, but the Green Bay Packers star got his first test of coaching on Friday night if he wants to get a head start on planning his post-playing career.
articles.body:
Jordan Love still has many years of playing in the NFL, but the Green Bay Packers star got his first test of coaching on Friday night if he wants to get a head start on planning his post-playing career.

Packers head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters Love called plays in the second half of their 42-38 win over the Arizona Cardinals and praised the "outstanding job" he did.

Since the Packers held out most of their starters, Love didn't have a lot to do otherwise. The offense was a little rough to start with just 12 yards on 10 plays and a lost fumble in the third quarter.

In the fourth quarter, though, everything started to click. The Packers outscored Arizona 18-7, scoring on all three offensive possessions.

articles.title: NFL restarts social justice messaging while battling domestic abuse, drunk driving and prostitution arrests
articles.summary: The NFL will bring back "Stop Hate" and "End Racism" end zone stencils for 2026 while facing a wave of player arrests and conduct investigations.
articles.body: The NFL will again during the 2026 season stencil its end zones and adorn helmets with "Stop Hate" or "End Racism" as part of its social justice messaging even as the league is inundated in arrests, court dates and personal conduct policy investigations having to do with criminal justice. The league wants to advance the message that every person deserves equal economic, political, and social rights, regardless of their background. And that's good. But it is not making any similar messaging push for stopping men getting physical with women, people driving under the influence or stopping human trafficking – even after one of its owners, Jed York of the San Francisco 49ers, got arrested by a human trafficking task force in Ohio in a prostitution sting. 49ERS OWNER JED YORK ARRESTED FOR 'ENGAGING IN PROSTITUTION' IN OHIO, PLEADS NO CONTEST TO LESSER CHARGES So the league is making social justice a priority while criminal justice needs addressing within its ranks. The return of the social justice push for 2026 was first reported by Front Office Sports. A league spokesman told OutKick that clubs will again have the opportunity to select their preferred end zone stencil messaging. The available options for 2026 for the clubs are the same as last year – "Choose Love," "Inspire Change," "End Racism" and "Stop Hate." Clubs can also use "Never Forget" on Week 1, which is in memoriam of the Sept. 11, 2001 terrorist attacks. Players can also again select from the four messages for their helmet decals throughout the season. Here's a thought: Any club not picking "Never Forget" on Week 1 is failing, regardless of what they pick the remainder of the season. Despite the NFL's social justice messaging on its fields and player helmets the rest of this year and every year since 2020, the FBI recorded a 51% increase in bias-motivated incidents from 2020 to 2024. The Anti-Defamation League recorded 2,024 antisemitic incidents in 2020, but by 2024 that number had risen to 9,354 — a more than fourfold increase. In 2020, the FBI reported 7,759 hate crimes. That number was at 10,881 in 2025. These rising statistics amid the NFL's social justice campaign is obviously not the league's fault, but it does raise the question whether its audience is the proper target. And if the league can continue a campaign that isn't necessarily stopping hate or racism, why can't it also take on the criminal problems that some of its own employees apparently have? NFL EMPLOYEES' TROUBLING DRIVING INCIDENTS MOUNT, COSTING JOBS AND PUTTING OTHERS AT RISK The two campaigns wouldn't have to be mutually exclusive. The NFL could stencil its end zones with "Stop drinking and driving" just as it will with one of the four options presented to teams for most of the season. The league could perhaps benefit from such messaging in its stadiums and on its helmets because DUI arrests or other traffic incidents involving NFL people are not uncommon. Consider: The Washington Commanders fired tight end coach Ben Steele on the eve of training camp following a DWI arrest in June. Defensive backs coach Gerald Alexander was suspended by the Minnesota Vikings after he pleaded guilty to third-degree DWI. The Los Angeles Chargers released guard Ben Cleveland after he was arrested on charges of speeding and driving with a limited permit. That arrest came roughly one-and-a-half-years removed from Cleveland being arrested for DUI. CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM Former Dallas Cowboys quarterback and current CBS NFL analyst Tony Romo was arrested in Wisconsin for OWI, which is Operating While Intoxicated, unsafe passing, open intoxicants and refusing a breathalyzer. A hearing is scheduled for Sept. 21. The NFL could also benefit from messaging that addresses domestic violence. The league has seen a not insignificant number of its players or others involved in domestic incidents this year. Just this week, Packers running back Josh Jacobs was charged with battery and one other misdemeanor count in an incident allegedly involving his ex-girlfriend. Falcons edge rusher James Pearce was suspended for the first eight games of the season after he was embroiled in a domestic incident and arrested in February. NFL PUTS 'INSPIRE CHANGE' AND 'CHOOSE LOVE' ON FIELDS BUT NOT SO AGGRESSIVE ABOUT ITS DOMESTIC ABUSE ISSUES Ravens receiver Rashod Bateman, Broncos linebacker Jonathon Cooper, Rams offensive lineman Alaric Jackson, and free agent receiver Tyreek Hill, also have run afoul of police or courts or both because of domestic issues this year. So, here's an end zone stencil idea the NFL should consider: "Tackle men but don't touch women." FOLLOW ARMANDO SALGUERO ON X: @ARMANDOSALGUERO

Raising kids to be able to hold a conversation with an adult and have the ability to read the room – Chris W. in California writes: I want to commend you for something you brought up in today's Screencaps about how you have done what you can to make sure your son knows how to handle himself when dealing with adults, etc. out in public. articles.title: Tua Tagovailoa Reacts to Boos From Dolphins Fans in Return to Miami with Falcons
articles.summary: Tua Tagovailoa wasn't greeted warmly by fans in South Beach as he made his first appearance against the Miami Dolphins in Friday's preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons.
articles.body:
Tua Tagovailoa wasn't greeted warmly by fans in South Beach as he made his first appearance against the Miami Dolphins in Friday's preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons.

After being booed by the crowd at Hard Rock Stadium when he took the field for the Falcons' first offensive possession, Tagovailoa told reporters he heard them but only recalled fond memories of his time in Miami:

"Well, of course I did. But, you know, needless to say, like, being able to come back here, like, I've had six years here, and those are probably some of the best six years of my life, being able to, you know, play for Miami, being able to be in front of the crowd.

"You know, I mean, [I] had a Pro Bowl here, like, had a good amount of accolades. So, regardless of the reaction, like, I mean, I love the city. We have a home out here. Like, we still have our house and whatnot. But, I mean, it is what it is. You know, I can't change any of what they did and whatnot, but, you know, it was really cool to see a lot of the guys after the game, and then, you know, talk to some of the guys during the game. So it was a cool homecoming, if you will."

Tagovailoa got the start and went 7-of-8 with 95 yards and lost a fumble in three possessions. He only played the first quarter in what was his best outing of the preseason.

The Dolphins released Tagovailoa in March, taking on the largest dead cap hit in NFL history as they completely tore down their roster under first-year head coach Jeff Hafley and general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan.

Atlanta signed Tagovailoa to a one-year contract in free agency with Michael Penix Jr. recovering from ACL surgery. Penix was recently cleared to take part in 11-on-11 drills in a significant step leading into the regular season.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski hasn't announced whether Tagovailoa or Penix will start in Week 1 against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Tagovailoa was originally drafted with the No. 5 overall pick by the Dolphins in 2020. He went 44-32 in 76 starts over six seasons with the club, leading them to playoff appearances in 2022 and 2023.

articles.title: Ravens Reportedly Trade DL to Giants Ahead of 2026 NFL Season, Full Return Revealed
articles.summary: With roster cutdown day approaching on Sunday, the Baltimore Ravens are trading defensive lineman C.J. Okoye to the New York Giants.
articles.body:
With roster cutdown day approaching on Sunday, the Baltimore Ravens are trading defensive lineman C.J. Okoye to the New York Giants.

Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport and Mike Garafolo , the Ravens will receive a 2028 seventh-round pick from the Giants in exchange for Okoye.

The Ravens are entering a new era with Jesse Minter as head coach. Even though he has previously worked on John Harbaugh's staff, Okoye was not on the team during his initial stint in Baltimore from 2017 to '20.

Okoye originally entered the NFL in 2022 through the international pathway program and had been projected to play offensive line. He was assigned to the Los Angeles Chargers in 2023, then switched to defense as a nose tackle.

In his first-ever appearance in an organized football game during the 2023 preseason, Okoye sacked Los Angeles Rams quarterback Stetson Bennett.

After not appearing in a regular-season game during his two years with the Chargers, Okoye signed a reserve/future contract with the Ravens in January 2025.

The Ravens signed Okoye to their practice squad before the start of last season. He was called up to the active roster and made his first appearance in Week 4 against the Kansas City Chiefs.

"I feel like I've still got more to do; I've still got more growing to do - but I'm learning right now and I'm picking it up. I feel like I've still got more to give and I just want to win," Okoye told ESPN's Leonard Solms in October 2025.

Okoye went on to appear in 13 games, recording 15 combined tackles and one quarterback hit. He found himself likely to be out of the defensive line rotation with Nnamdi Madubuike returning after an injury-plagued 2025 and Rayshaun Benny added as a late-round draft pick this year.

He is going to a place in the Giants with a head coach that knows him very well and can offer him playing time. Their defensive interior prior to the trade included Shelby Harris, D.J. Reader, Josh Tupou, sixth-round rookie Bobby Jamison-Travis and undrafted rookies Anquin Barnes Jr. and Ben Barten.

Okoye at least gives the Giants a wild-card player with upside to boost their defensive tackle play, particularly as they try to shore up a run defense that allowed the second-most rushing yards in the NFL last season.

articles.title: New Fantasy Football 2026 QB, RB, WR, TE Rankings and Top Sleepers
articles.summary: With the 2026 NFL preseason drawing to a close, fantasy managers have entered the prime drafting window. While some roster surprises may still occur, we have a pretty good idea of how depth charts and player roles are going to look entering the regular season.
articles.body:
With the 2026 NFL preseason drawing to a close, fantasy managers have entered the prime drafting window. While some roster surprises may still occur, we have a pretty good idea of how depth charts and player roles are going to look entering the regular season.

We also have a better idea of who some of this year's top sleepers could be, based on that aforementioned information.

Here, you'll find some updated point-per-reception (PPR) rankings for the key offensive positions, along with some potential sleepers to target.

Sleeper: Jordan Love, QB, Green Bay Packers

The Green Bay Packers are still waiting for quarterback Jordan Love to break into the ranks of the elite. There's a very real chance that it'll finally happen in 2026. Love is coming off his best season as a full-time starter in terms of efficiency (101.2 QB rating) and is looking to be a stronger finisher.

Love also has a terrific supporting cast, albeit one that has seen some shuffling this offseason. He finished last season as QB15 despite making only 15 starts, and he could see a jump into the top 10 this year.

At worst, Love should be a strong streamer, and with an average draft position (ADP) of 137 , he should provide great value on draft day.

Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers

Sleeper: Kenneth Gainwell, RB, Tampa Bay Buccaneers

Kenneth Gainwell joined the Pittsburgh Steelers last offseason and went on to have a career year. Despite splitting time with Jaylen Warren, he finished as RB15 in PPR leagues.

After Gainwell moved on to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the spring, managers seem to have forgotten about him. He'll split time with Bucky Irving in Tampa but is much more valuable than his ADP of 90 .

Gainwell will be especially valuable in PPR leagues, as he's looking like a significant piece of Tampa's passing attack. According to Adam Slivon of Pewter Report, Gainwell got a lot of work as a receiver out of the backfield in early training camp.

Sleeper: Ja'Kobi Lane, WR, Baltimore Ravens

Rookie wide receivers regularly provide solid fantasy value, and every year, one selected in the later rounds proves to be a legitimate steal.

Third-round pick Ja'Kobi Lane is looking like he could be the steal of 2026. The USC product has been arguably the biggest star of Baltimore Ravens camp, and he should quickly become one of Lamar Jackson's go-to targets.

"Few Ravens have ever made as good a first impression," The Athletic's Jeff Zrebiec wrote. "Lane's acrobatic and seemingly effortless catches have enthralled a fan base obsessed with the idea of a dynamic homegrown receiving corps."

It's worth noting that Baltimore will probably feature a run-heavy offense, even under a new coaching staff. However, Lane has massive sleeper potential with an ADP of just 171 .

Sleeper: Isaiah Likely, TE, New York Giants

The Ravens have a new coaching staff because they fired Josh Harbaugh following the 2025 season. Harbaugh quickly landed with the New York Giants, and he was soon followed by tight end Isaiah Likely.

In Baltimore, Likely played the TE2 role behind Mark Andrews, but he was still a solid fantasy option when the offense was clicking. In 2024, for example, he caught 42 passes for 477 yards and six touchdowns.

In New York, Likely will be the TE1 and one of Jaxson Dart's top targets—especially since the Giants have questionable receiver depth behind Malik Nabers. Likely has an ADP of just 104 .

articles.title: What does Tom Brady save from each of his 7 Super Bowl wins? His answer has nothing to do with rings
articles.summary: NFL News: Seven Super Bowl championships gave Tom Brady enough hardware to fill a room. The memories he deliberately saved, however, fit on his phone.Brady rece.
articles.body: Seven Super Bowl championships gave Tom Brady enough hardware to fill a room. The memories he deliberately saved, however, fit on his phone.Brady recently revealed that he created folders for his Super Bowl victories and kept the congratulatory messages people sent him after each championship. According to Brady’s YouTube QnA video posted months ago, on Feb. 8, the former New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback has maintained the unusual digital archive for years.What does Tom Brady keep from each of his seven Super Bowl championships?Brady showed the system while discussing how he preserves memories from his career.“You know what's pretty cool, let me show you my phone,” Brady said. “I have kept file folders. I file everything.”Those folders contain messages sent to Brady following his championship wins. Rather than leaving the texts buried in years of conversations, he saved them separately.“I keep all the amazing messages that people sent me. I wanted to keep them as great memories,” Brady said.It is a collection tied to a résumé no other NFL quarterback has matched.Brady appeared in 10 Super Bowls and won seven of them. He also earned five Super Bowl MVP awards. His championship run began with the Patriots following the 2001 season and eventually extended to the Buccaneers, where he won his seventh title nearly two decades later.Each victory brought another wave of messages and another folder.“Congratulations and a lot of really cool ones over the years,” Brady said. “It's such a special moment and you always want to remember.”The detail offers a different look at how Brady cataloged those seasons. The public record contains the scores, statistics, trophies and game footage. His phone contains something those records cannot recreate: what people close to him were saying immediately after the wins.That also explains why simply calling the folders “memorabilia” misses the point. Brady did not collect another physical object from the games. He preserved conversations tied directly to those moments.Why have Tom Brady’s saved messages become such a unique record of his NFL career?Brady spent more than two decades building one of the most decorated careers in NFL history. That makes the timeline inside those folders unusually long.The first messages date back to the beginning of his championship run with New England. The later ones followed titles won after Brady had already become one of the NFL’s biggest names. His final championship came with Tampa Bay, giving the archive material from different teams and different stages of his career.The folders also preserve something championship rings cannot: the people surrounding each moment.Messages sent after a Super Bowl can come from teammates, coaches, friends, family members and others connected to a player. Brady did not identify every person represented in his folders in the comments per the video, so the contents remain private. What he did explain was why he kept them.He wanted the memories.That makes the habit particularly fitting for a career defined by repetition at the highest level. Brady did not win one Super Bowl and preserve one extraordinary night. He had to create the system again and again.His organizational habits were also well documented throughout his playing career. Brady entered the NFL as a sixth-round draft pick before spending more than 20 seasons building routines around preparation, film study and training. Saving and sorting championship messages follows the same basic instinct: keep track of what matters instead of assuming it will always be easy to find later.There is also a simple difference between a record and a memory.Brady’s seven championships, 10 appearances and five Super Bowl MVP awards will remain in NFL record books. The messages capture what those achievements felt like to the people communicating with him when they happened.Years after his final NFL season, Brady can still open a folder and return to those conversations.For a quarterback whose career is usually reduced to rings and records, that may be the most interesting part of the collection. He already knows what he won. His phone helps him remember who was there to celebrate it.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Mecole Hardman Jr. Reportedly Cut by Bills, Top Potential Landing Spots in NFL Free Agency
articles.summary: The Buffalo Bills plan to release veteran wide receiver and return man Mecole Hardman Jr., according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills plan to release veteran wide receiver and return man Mecole Hardman Jr., according to ESPN's Jeremy Fowler .

Hardman, 28, entered the NFL in 2019 and has played seven seasons with the Kansas City Chiefs, New York Jets and Bills.

A third stint with the Chiefs could potentially be an option for Hardman following his release, or he could land with a team that struggled on punt returns last season, such as the Green Bay Packers, Las Vegas Raiders or Los Angeles Chargers.

Originally selected by the Chiefs in the second round of the 2019 NFL draft, Hardman was named a Pro Bowler and Second Team All-Pro as a rookie thanks to his 26.1-yard kick return average and one kick return touchdown.

Hardman also topped the 500-yard receiving mark in each of his first three NFL seasons, but he is best known for catching the game-winning touchdown in overtime of the Chiefs' Super Bowl LVIII win over the San Francisco 49ers.

In 82 career regular-season games, Hardman has caught 178 passes for 2,302 yards and 16 touchdowns. He has also rushed for three touchdowns and scored one touchdown each on kick and punt returns.

Following a stint on their practice squad, Hardman was elevated to appear in two regular-season games for the Bills last season. He did not catch a pass, but he had a 61-yard kick return and returned two punts for a total of four yards.

In two playoff games, Hardman had one catch for four yards and a touchdown, and he had a 22-yard kick return.

Hardman remained with the Bills entering this year's training camp in hopes of winning a roster spot as a punt returner and depth wide receiver.

The Bills already have a First Team All-Pro kick returner in running back Ray Davis, but he has yet to show a propensity for punt returns.

In fact, Davis muffed a punt and the Pittsburgh Steelers recovered it during the Bills' preseason finale on Thursday, leading to speculation that Hardman could potentially make the team.

However, the Bills are reportedly moving on from Hardman anyway, and they will have to find a different answer for the punt return spot.

articles.title: Fantasy Football 2026 Ranking Sleepers, Busts and Safest Players This Year
articles.summary: When ever you wind up making your fantasy draft picks—and, given the proximity to the 2026 NFL season's opening kick, it'll surely happen soon—think of each selection as its own value proposition.
articles.body:
When ever you wind up making your fantasy draft picks—and, given the proximity to the 2026 NFL season's opening kick, it'll surely happen soon—think of each selection as its own value proposition.

The aim, of course, is to maximize the value of each pick and ideally build such a surplus that you cruise to a comfortable title run.

So, the goal is just to snatch up all of the league's top players, right? We can only wish. Since everyone else is aiming for the same, you're going to have to take some risks and hope enough pan out to give you a realistic championship chance.

The actual goal, then, involves limiting exposure to bottom-out bust risks, snagging some low-ish-risk, high-reward sleepers and adding some insurance policies by way of "safe" selections (picking players who consistently deliver results). We're here to help you identify all three with our top sleeper, bust and safe calls at the three marquee positions.

Quarterback: Kyler Murray, Arizona Cardinals ( ADP: 155 overall, QB17)

If Murray stays on the field, he produces. During the four seasons in which he made 14-plus appearances, he always cleared 3,700 passing yards with 20-plus touchdowns. He also never rushed for fewer than 423 yards or four scores. With Kevin O'Connell as his playcaller, and Justin Jefferson, Jordan Addison and Jauan Jennings filling out the receiver ranks, Murray could be a fantasy gold mine.

Running back: Rachaad White, Washington Commanders ( ADP: 120 overall, RB42)

White's rushing impact can vary, but he's always a factor in the passing game (205 receptions for 1,450 yards and 11 scores over four seasons). It's hard to imagine things won't stay the same—if not improve—in Washington given his connection with quarterback Jayden Daniels (a teammate for two seasons at Arizona State) and limited target competition from starter Jacory Croskey-Merritt (nine receptions as a rookie).

Wide receiver: De'Zhaun Stribling, San Francisco 49ers ( ADP: 176 overall, WR55)

Stribling has been one of the league's buzziest players since the start of training camp, and while that might make you worry about overdoing expectations, the reality is there's just too much to like about his talent, athletic profile and situation. The 49ers offense has its share of name-brand playmakers, but they're almost all on the wrong side of 30 and already dealing with availability concerns.

*standard-league average draft position (ADP) data courtesy of FantasyPros

Quarterback: Jayden Daniels, Washington Commanders ( ADP: 68 overall, QB5)

The risk here isn't the player—it's the price. As the fifth quarterback off the board, it's almost like the fantasy community is denying the existence of Daniels' rough, injury-riddled 2025 season. This price tag puts a ton of pressure on him to perform as a passer, since Washington could limit his usage as a designed runner in hopes of keeping him healthy. Plus, the collection of playmakers gets pretty dicey after Terry McLaurin and Stefon Diggs.

Running back: Christian McCaffrey, San Francisco 49ers ( ADP: 4 overall, RB17)

There's definitely a chance McCaffrey makes this look silly. There's also a chance he only makes it through a handful of games, just as he did the last two seasons after handling 330-plus touches (seven games combined). His touch count reached a ridiculous 450 in 2025 (playoffs included). That's an ominous number for anyone, let alone a 30-year-old running back with his injury history and some question marks on the offensive line in front of him.

Wide receiver: Alec Pierce, Indianapolis Colts ( ADP: 97 overall, WR37)

Pierce has been a true home-run hitter the past two seasons (yards-per-catch leader in both), but will he have the same juice after a bumpy recovery from offseason ankle surgery? He figures to be slow (if not sidelined) out of the gate, and the worry is he'll be trying to play catch-up for the entire campaign. Throw in increased target competition from the recent signing of veteran Keenan Allen and some lingering questions about quarterback Daniel Jones, and Pierce carries more risk than his draft cost would imply.

Quarterback: Matthew Stafford, Los Angeles Rams ( ADP: 123 overall, QB12)

Here is the entirety of Stafford's concern list for his 2026 fantasy outlook: He is 38 years old. Counterpoint: He was 37 last season, when he obliterated opposing defenses to the tune of 4,707 passing yards and 46 touchdown passes en route to his first MVP award. Respecting a repeat of that production is asking for trouble, but his draft cost includes zero tax on his upside. Between L.A.'s playcalling and pass-catching talent, Stafford feels like a set-him-and-forget-him weekly starter.

Running back: Chase Brown, Cincinnati Bengals ( ADP: 16 overall, RB9)

Brown might be relatively new to the scene as a member of the 2023 draft class, but he is already becoming the model of consistency. He had 283 touches and 1,350 scrimmage yards in 2024, and then 301 touches for 1,456 scrimmage yards in 2025, scoring exactly 11 touchdowns in each campaign. The Bengals might have their best offensive line of Brown's tenure, and if they do, this offense could be the NFL's best.

Wide receiver: Amon-Ra St. Brown, Detroit Lions ( ADP: 155 overall, QB17)

Last season, St. Brown finished as WR3 in all of fantasy. Just like he did in 2024 —and 2023 , too. Anyone sensing a pattern here? Everything about his profile screams "safe," and not in the way that indicates a lack of upside. Things might happen in football, but he feels pretty guaranteed for greatness after averaging 117 receptions for 1,393 yards and 11 touchdowns over this stretch.

articles.title: Updated Jaxson Dart Fantasy Outlook 2026: Giants QB Competing For the NFC East Crown
articles.summary: Jaxson Dart enters his second NFL season with the New York Giants carrying immense fantasy upside after a highly productive rookie campaign. Last season, Dar...
articles.body:
Jaxson Dart enters his second NFL season with the New York Giants carrying immense fantasy upside after a highly productive rookie campaign. Last season, Dart finished as a top-12 fantasy QB1 in the majority of his full games, proving he can already be a reliable weekly starter for fantasy managers in a year where the injury bug couldn't be avoided.

Should I Draft Jaxson Dart in Fantasy Football?

What makes that baseline so incredibly encouraging is the context of his surrounding cast. Dart achieved that high-end fantasy production with just three of his targets for the season going to Malik Nabers, a receiver who very well could be one of the best of this generation. Having a healthy Nabers (the next negative report out of camp for him will be the first) back on the perimeter this year radically raises the ceiling of this entire passing attack and gives Dart a true alpha target.

The ultimate driver of Dart's fantasy value remains his rushing equity near the goal line. At one point last year, he had an incredible run with five straight games with a rushing touchdown. While a streak like that is highly unlikely to happen again, the simple fact that it can happen is more than enough to make us happy and solidify his weekly floor.

When you combine that rushing threat with his arm, the volume is undeniably elite. In 2025, no player in the NFL had more games with 25+ pass attempts AND a rushing touchdown. Dart recorded five such games as a rookie, matching the totals of only Josh Allen, Patrick Mahomes, and Trevor Lawrence. Draft Dart with confidence as an ascending dual-threat QB1 who possesses genuine league-winning upside in his sophomore season.

Savvy managers will keep tabs on the waiver wire, understanding that Dart's style can make him a flight risk. You don't have to get ready if you stay ready in terms of a contingency plan, so as long as you're comfortable signing up for that, the light is green in the draft room.

On the whole, this is a player whose ceiling we don't fully understand and that makes him a fun buy for those willing to do the work should his play style again result in DNPs.

articles.title: Patriots make first reported cuts ahead of 53-man roster deadline
articles.summary: A total of 13 players have been let go during the first wave of roster cuts.
articles.body:
Coming out of their preseason finale and heading into the weekend, the New England Patriots had an active roster of 91 players. With the cutdown deadline looming, they have started trimming that number.

The team started by informing 13 players of their release . Wide receivers Kyle Dixon, Nick DeGennaro and Cameron Dorner, tight end C.J. Dippre, offensive tackle Lorenz Metz, interior offensive linemen Darrian Dalcourt, Jacob Rizy and JonDarius Morgan, outside linebackers Xavier Holmes and Amari Gainer, and cornerbacks Brandon Crossley and Marcellas Dial Jr. have all been waived, according to multiple reports.

In addition, the team released safety Eric Butler with an injury designation.

Dixon, 25, started his college career as a baseball player before returning to the gridiron with Culver-Stockton in 2024. In two seasons and 22 games with the Wildcats, he caught 143 passes for 2,394 yards and 24 touchdowns. A two-time first-team All-HAAC selection, he went unselected in this year's draft. Joining the Patriots as a rookie free agent in May, he caught a team-leading 10 passes for 81 yards in the preseason.

DeGennaro, 25, played college football at Maryland, Richmond and James Madison. Despite his experience and a 4.40-second 40-yard dash, he took the free agency route to the NFL and New England specifically. A depth option throughout the summer, he ended up playing in three preseason games and caught five passes for 65 yards and a touchdown.

Dorner, 22, began his college career at Division II Shepherd University before a one-year stint at North Texas. Despite some solid production in his lone season in Division I, he was not selected in this year's draft. He joined the Patriots as a UDFA, and in three preseason games caught four passes for 37 yards.

Dippre, 24, spent his college career at Alabama before arriving in New England as a rookie free agent last offseason. Initially a practice squad player, he was promoted to the 53-man roster in November to prevent other teams from poaching him. He eventually finished the year on the active team and played a combined 46 snaps on offense and special teams over his two in-game appearances. Dippre started this year's training camp on the PUP list, and caught two preseason passes for 21 yards after his return.

Metz, 29, started his football career at the amateur level in Germany. He later played college football in Cincinnati and through stints with the Bears and Buccaneers found his way to New England in 2025. An exempt practice squad player due to his international status, he was re-signed by the team in the offseason and carried on the roster as a 91st player.

Dalcourt, 25, also played college football at Alabama. He joined the Ravens as a rookie free agent in 2024 and via subsequent stints in Washington, Carolina and Cleveland made his way to New England. He played 25 offensive snaps over his two preseason appearances as a Patriot.

Rizy, 24, spent his six-year college career at Harvard and Florida State, where he started 27 total games and saw action all over the offensive line. He ultimately did not get selected in the 2026 NFL Draft, but made his way to Foxborough shortly thereafter. Serving as the Patriots' third-string center, he played 155 preseason snaps and started the finale against the Browns.

Morgan, 23, entered the NFL off of college stints at South Carolina and UAB. The rookie free agent signing ended up appearing in three of the Patriots' preseason games, but was on the field for only 40 combined snaps as a third-string option at guard.

Holmes, 24, split his college career between Maine and James Madison. He did not hear his name called in this year's draft and instead joined the Patriots as a rookie free agent two weeks later. While he did show some flashes early in camp, an undisclosed injury has kept him out for the last few weeks and prevented him from appearing in any preseason games.

Gainer, 26, played at Florida State and North Carolina before joining the Raiders as a rookie free agent in 2024. He arrived in New England during the 2025 season as a practice squad player and was later signed to a futures contract for 2026. He provided edge depth during the summer and registered one sack in three preseason contests.

Crossley, 25, spent six years in college. The Colorado State and SMU product, who was an All-ACC honorable mention in his final season, did not hear his name called in the 2025 NFL Draft. He signed with the Patriots as a free agent shortly thereafter and spent his rookie campaign on and off their practice squad without seeing any game action. He was brought back this year as a depth piece at cornerback.

Dial Jr, 25, played college football at Georgia Military and South Carolina. He was then selected in the sixth round of the 2024 NFL Draft by the Patriots and remained the last player from that class alongside Drake Maye. He is being let go with 17 in-game appearances and one start to his name, all coming during his rookie season. This summer, he served as a depth nickel back.

Butler, 23, went unselected in this year's draft and earned rookie minicamp invitations with the Raiders and Saints. The San Diego State product remained unsigned until arriving in New England in early August, however. If he clears waivers, he will revert to the Patriots' injured reserve list.

With the first 13 moves now reported, New England's roster stands at 78 players. The team will have to move below the league-mandated 53-man threshold by 6 p.m. ET on Sunday, Aug. 30.
